outcome: The work item page shows live work, and the shared workspace can read any line through an adapter
acceptance_criteria: Opening `/work/4102` against the mock (Next 4980, mock 4981) shows the title, a "Processing" state tag, the next step, and "Drafting the weekly update" as the activity line; no station track, six facts strip or agent steps are on the page, and no "not available" text appears — verify: open the page and view the DOM; `frontend/e2e/work-item.spec.ts` asserts those three parts are absent.

The same page against live Django (8020, Postgres 55433, account live-lead) for a real work id shows the live `title`, `status_label`, `next_step` and `blocker`, matching `GET /api/v1/work/{id}` — verify: compare the page with `oa.py live GET /api/v1/work/{work_id} 3` output and the JSON from `curl` with the session.

The page makes no request to the v7 mock-only fields: its code imports the `WorkItem` type from the live schema and not from `@/api/schema` — verify: `grep -rn "api/schema'" frontend/src/features/work-item` returns nothing for work item types.

While `current_activity.watching` is true the page re-reads every 5 s; with `watching:false` and a state other than `processing` it makes one read only; a hidden tab pauses reads — verify: unit test `useWorkItem` with fake timers; in the browser network panel count `GET /work/4102` calls.

A failed poll keeps the last good item on screen and shows the "couldn't refresh" note; a 401, 403 or 404 on a poll replaces the page with the matching state and stops polling — verify: unit test with a mocked client.

`/work/4106` (mock) and a live id the account cannot see both show exactly "This record is unavailable." with no difference between them — verify: open both and compare the text; unit test on the 404 body.

A 403 with `code:'csrf_failed'` does not show "Your account can't use PSL Factory" or the no-access state; it refreshes the session and says to try again — verify: mock scenario `csrf_failed` plus unit test.
A 401 shows the signed-out state with a link to `/sign-in?next=` the current path — verify: sign out in the mock, open `/work/4102`, click the link.

Decisions waiting (`/work/4103`) show one row with its role and status and an "Open decision" link to `/work/4103/decide?task=<id>` only when `can_decide` or `can_claim` is true; a row with both false has no link; the page makes no claim or decision call — verify: e2e plus network panel.
A verified item (`/work/4101`) shows an "Open the output" link equal to `output_url`; an item with `output_url:null` shows none — verify: e2e on both fixtures.
A null `revision` or `case_revision` (`/work/4104`, `/work/4105`) is not rendered as 0 and the page loads — verify: e2e plus unit test on the item mapper.

`/work/4101/history` lists rows from `GET /work/{id}/history`; the Decisions, Agent work and Evidence tabs call it with `kind=decision`, `worker` and `evidence`; no counts and no "show more" are drawn; the caption reads "Showing the latest 30 changes. As of …" only when 30 rows came back — verify: unit and e2e tests; network panel.
A history row with an unknown `station` or `status` shows the raw text; a row without `actor` shows no actor; an `evidence_id` of null shows no evidence link — verify: unit test on the row mapper.
History empty shows "No changes recorded yet."; a history error shows the mapped message with Try again and keeps the chosen tab — verify: mock scenarios and e2e.

No write button (Resume, Cancel, Check what happened, Release, Start, Correct) appears on the page, and no `POST` other than the file upload is made by anything in this feature — verify: e2e asserts no such buttons; grep `liveApi.POST` in the new files shows only the upload and the picker's proposal calls.

`src/features/workspace/adapter.ts` exports `PanelRef`, `LineContext`, `LineAdapter`, `CommandDescriptor`, `registerLineAdapter`, `adapterFor` as specified, and a test registers a fake adapter, reads its panel, gets `Section[]` that the existing `Sections` renderer draws, and gets a `CommandDescriptor` whose `body()` includes the action, the tokens and a uuid key — verify: `adapter.test.ts`; typecheck passes.
A `null` token in a descriptor stays `null` in `body()`; a line with no key field gives `idempotency.field === null` and no key in the body — verify: `adapter.test.ts`.

`/work/4102` renders the weekly report panel through the adapter: the period, the four parts with "N records cited", the recipients with their receipt state, and `next_action`; a recipient with `receipt_id:null` reads "No receipt yet"; a null `editable_parts` and `draft` show no parts section — verify: e2e on 4102 and unit test on `weeklyReportAdapter`.
Against live Django, a weekly report work item's panel shows the same period and recipients as `GET /api/v1/work/{id}/weekly-report` — verify: compare the page with the `curl` JSON.
A `panels[]` entry whose key has no registered adapter does not break the page: it is omitted or shown as a link, and the rest of the page loads — verify: unit test with an unknown key.
The weekly report descriptor for `correct` is returned with `disabledReason` set when `can_correct` is false, and is not rendered as a button — verify: unit test and e2e (no button).

The picker uploads a PDF to `POST /cases/{case_id}/files` as multipart and returns the `upload_id`; the same call against live Django returns 200 with `upload_id`, `name`, `size`, `sha256` — verify: unit test against the mock; a live check with `live-lead` on a case they may write to, shown by the returned JSON.
The picker refuses a `.exe` and a file over 10 MB before any request is sent, and shows the file row's error with Try again — verify: unit test asserts no fetch call.

Upload errors map as specified: mock scenarios 413, 415, 422 (with `fields`), 429, 404 and a dropped network each show their own wording, and a failed upload is not retried until Try again is pressed — verify: unit tests; count fetch calls.
A 403 `csrf_failed` during upload refreshes the session once and says "Press upload again"; no automatic second upload — verify: unit test counts fetch calls (one upload, one session read).
The picker's types keep `UploadId` and `EvidenceId` distinct: assigning an `UploadId` where an `EvidenceId` is expected fails typecheck — verify: a `// @ts-expect-error` test in `evidence.test.ts`.

`fileToEvidence` calls the drafts route, then the review route, and returns `reviewed_evidence_id`; a null result is returned as null and the code and the PR description label it "proposal, backend question 1" — verify: unit test against the mock; grep for the label.
The picker and the proposal are not rendered by any page and the PR lists them as unused-by-design until F-87 — verify: grep for `EvidencePicker` imports shows only tests.
The picker uploads only to the loaded item's `case_id`; there is no input for a case id — verify: component test and props type.

Viewport check at 1440 and 390: the page matches the SCR-02 work item boards for the parts that remain (header, tag, next step, decisions waiting, output link); the hidden parts leave no empty gap or empty heading — verify: screenshots at both widths reviewed against `design/screens.md` SCR-02 artboards.

`npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass, and `api-live-schema-drift.test.ts` still passes with `live-schema.d.ts` regenerated from contract 1.22.0 — verify: `delivery/checks.sh` result.

risk.rationale: Medium. The work touches shared workspace code that lanes A and B build on, and it fixes a cross-layer contract (the adapter and command descriptor shapes). The picker uploads files to case evidence, which is a security surface. Money, identity and migrations are not touched, since all writes are deferred to F-87. Product acceptance is required because the page hides approved design parts, which changes what the client sees.

findings.summary: `makeCommand` body spreads `...inputs` last (`adapter.ts` body()), so a caller's inputs could override `action`, the revision tokens or the key. Lane A and B should not pass those names, or the spread should come first. No current caller does.

The history `evidence_id` is drawn as the text "Evidence N" with no link (`LiveWorkItemView.tsx`, History). The spec says "evidence link"; no evidence page route exists yet, so this is acceptable until one does.

In `ErrorState`, a 403 `csrf_failed` on a read shows "Refresh your session and try again." without calling `refreshSession()` itself. `call()` does refresh on csrf (`client.ts:64`) when `refreshOnCsrf` is set, so the behaviour is covered. Confirm the page's read uses that default.
The breadcrumb shows the raw line key ("WEEKLY_REPORT", "INVOICE"). Use a plain business label when the line is known. LiveWorkItemView.tsx Header.

Decision rows show raw lowercase words ("review · PMO Lead · open"). The second row ("approval · Finance Lead") has no link and no reason, so it reads like a dead end. Capitalise the words and say who it is waiting on. LiveWorkItemView.tsx Overview.
The history row shows "Evidence 11" as plain text. The spec says a link when evidence_id is set. Link it when an evidence route exists, otherwise record the gap.
While a line panel loads, it draws nothing (PanelView returns null). Add a small loading line so the page does not seem to finish early.

The breadcrumb prints raw identifiers ("MY_WORK / WEEKLY_REPORT / WORK 4102", underscores visible) where the board shows the plain reference and project ("INV-0412 · LAGOON HEALTH"). Use plain words (replace underscores with spaces, or show the project title); see LiveWorkItemView.tsx crumb.
State tag sits beside the title; the board puts it right-aligned on the title row. Taste only, same as the v7 frame on other pages if it matches there.

item.output_url is put straight into an anchor href with no scheme check (LiveWorkItemView.tsx:229-233). The value comes from the backend, so it is trusted today. A javascript: or data: value would still run on click. Suggest allowing only a same-origin path or https, and adding rel="noopener" if the link can leave the site.

Criteria 7 and 8 could not be driven end to end in the browser. The mock scenario cookie applies to every route, so the app shell's /me or /session read fails first: scenario 401 shows the shell's "You're signed out. Sign-in opens in a later release." (no /sign-in?next link, expected on this base before F-58) and scenario csrf_failed shows the shell's "We couldn't load your account", never the work page's own wording. Those work-page states rest on the builder's unit tests, which I did not re-run. Re-check once F-58 and a per-route scenario are in.

Weekly report period end is shown in the browser's zone: end_at 2026-11-22T23:59:59Z reads "To 23 Nov 00:59" (zone UTC+1). A week that ends Sunday reads as Monday. The period is a business range, so the design engineer may want it shown as the end day. Not a spec break.

Mock scenario 500 leaves /work/4102 loading normally (route not covered by the scenario for the 500 case), so the plain-server-error wording of the page was not seen. 429 ("Try again shortly.", Try again) and 503 ("Try again shortly.", Try again) were seen.

Live proof is missing for criteria 2, 19 and the live half of 22: live `title`, `status_label`, `next_step` and `blocker`, the live weekly report panel, and a live `POST /cases/{case_id}/files` returning `upload_id`, `name`, `size` and `sha256`. Expected: compared against live Django (8020, Postgres 55433). Actual: unproved (no seeded work item, no storage, no login). The mock evidence and contract checks are enough for this slice's delivery acceptance. Before any live claim, or before F-87's writes are accepted live, these must be proved: (a) seed a work item and a weekly-report item for `live-lead` and compare the page with `oa.py live GET /api/v1/work/{id}` and `/weekly-report`; (b) start object storage and upload one PDF through the picker on a case the account may write to; (c) a signed-in 404 and 403 on live must read the same "This record is unavailable." The status of this feature and its parent package must say "mock-proved, live pending" until then.

Criterion 3 is met for `src/features/work-item/live/` only. The v7 files in `src/features/work-item/` still import `@/api/schema` for `W-` ids, by the builder's recorded choice. Do not read criterion 3 as the whole `work-item` folder. The v7 frame and its dispatch must be removed when the last line has moved (`build.md`, notes for the coordinator).

Criteria 7 and 8 (csrf_failed and 401 wording on the work page) rest on unit tests. QA could not drive them in the browser (QA-1-1), and the sign-in link depends on F-58. Re-check once F-58 and a per-route mock scenario are in. Criterion 30 compared the page with the boards by eye only, and the design-fidelity tool was not run on this slice. The `fidelity/` folder holds the reports and side-by-side images for SCR-02. The UI review covers them, and the hidden board parts are the named exceptions.
